A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SAPT/STSS framework, renamed from TLLA to FGA. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including material moved into v2's appendices.

before.justification: V1 reports original classification experiments with two CLIP backbones, component ablations, hyperparameter sensitivity and loss-landscape case studies.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental results and adds benchmark comparisons, runtime and memory measurements, and perturbation-count sensitivity results.

M1.justification: FGA retains SAPT, random-perturbation scoring of augmented views, and voting without test-time parameter updates. V2 explicitly introduces a balancing weight λ but fixes it to 1, recovering v1's loss-plus-sharpness formulation. The expanded equations do not establish a changed operational procedure.

E1.justification: Cross-dataset coverage expands from seven targets to ten for ViT-B/16, adding Food101, UCF101 and EuroSAT, covering additional food, action and remote-sensing categories. ResNet50 adds Food101 and UCF101 in Appendix C. ImageNet and its four distribution-shift variants remain.

E2.justification: V2 Table 1 adds MTA, TDA, DPE, SAR+CoOp and CoOp-initialized C-TPT, ZERO and MTA comparisons. Table 2 newly includes C-TPT, ZERO and TDA in cross-dataset evaluation, alongside additional CoOp/MaPLe combinations. These substantially expand comparator membership beyond v1.

E3.justification: V1 selects both perturbation radii by grid search; v2 fixes test-time ρ′=0.5 while retaining the training-radius search. This is a reported protocol revision, without evidence establishing reruns. New experiments include single-sample-adapted SAR and latency/peak-memory evaluation on a V100; the original training budgets and augmentation setup remain.

E4.justification: Appendix D.2 adds sensitivity to perturbation count R, reporting fluctuations below 0.5% for R≥4. V2 also supplies per-dataset component-ablation results in Table 1. The existing perturbation-radius/retention analysis and loss-landscape case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports empirical repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new perturbation-count sweep is sensitivity analysis, not uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: V2 adds numerous dataset/comparator results and reports FGA's 0.07 seconds per image and 4.14 GB memory usage. Existing values also change: the ViT DiffTPT average is corrected from 62.28 to 62.58, and STSS+CoOp changes from 66.50 to 66.48. Full-method accuracies on retained datasets remain unchanged; its cross-dataset ViT average changes from 67.90 to 67.60 because coverage expands from seven to ten datasets.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 changes from a scalar, pointwise loss bound using FΔF discrepancy to a vector-valued expected-loss bound using twice total variation, with a new vector-contraction argument. Theorem 4 and Appendix B add quantile terms, positive-probability assumptions, and an explicit entropy/cross-entropy error bound and proof, replacing v1's informal surrogate-error remark.

C1.justification: V2 replaces the broad emphasis on backpropagation being unnecessary with a claim that training-history-blind adaptation is suboptimal and training flatness can jointly guide training and testing. The central contributions—flatness-guided sample selection, efficient adaptation and improved generalization—remain.

C2.justification: V2 explains STSS's effectiveness without SAPT through SGD's implicit preference for flat minima, qualifies comparisons between single-sample and online adaptation, and explains why relative sharpness permits few perturbations. Its new future-work discussion identifies the retained TPT-style setup as the tested scope and leaves broader architectures and objectives unvalidated.

D1.justification: V2 discloses R=16, retention of 10% of views, λ=1, fixed ρ′=0.5 and V100 hardware, and supplies upstream CoOp/TPT repository links and license information. Most training details already existed in v1. V1's prospective code-release statement disappears; v2 does not establish availability of the proposed method's own implementation.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially refines positioning by discussing SAR and SoTTA's test-time sharpness optimization and distinguishing FGA's training/testing interaction from them, replacing v1's first-study assertion. It adds online cache/prototype methods, SAM variants and newer generalization work; the revised proof also introduces Maurer's vector-contraction reference.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, method explanations and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting around the training/testing flatness narrative. TLLA becomes FGA, SAPT/STSS receive numbered subsections, and the appendices gain an overview, results, reproducibility and LLM-use sections. Title, authorship and affiliation text also change.

P2.justification: The document is extensively reformatted from a two-column layout to a predominantly single-column conference layout. Figure 2 is redrawn, the component-ablation bar chart is replaced by table rows, and combined-backbone tables are split between the main text and Appendix C. Tables expand and the sensitivity plot is restyled; existing landscape illustrations are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation of the central contribution: Section 5.2 supplies comparative runtime and memory evidence absent from v1, Tables 1–4 broaden coverage and strengthen comparisons, and Appendix D supplies important missing reproduction settings. The theory explicitly addresses the entropy-surrogate gap, although Equation 11's 2μ coefficient disagrees with Equation 60's 2√2μ coefficient. Empirical uncertainty remains unreported, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial gains in evidence and reproducibility.
